text:
Dawn on 14 March 2031 found Brannock Harbour wrapped in a thin grey mist, the kind the old pilots used to call "strait breath." Out of it, slowly, came the hull of the Isolde, white and broad against the water.

The Halvorsen Strait Ferry Authority has spent years debating how to replace its ageing crossings, and the argument has often been about size. Yesterday's ceremony settled it, at least on paper. The Isolde, lead vessel of a new class, was formally accepted into service that day.

Captain Marguerite Olvanger, the Authority's Fleet Operations Director, confirmed at the handover that the ship carries 1,800 passengers. It can also take 420 vehicles across two decks. The figures appear in the Certificate of Passenger Capacity, Ref. HSFA-IC-0147, issued after the acceptance trials at Brannock.

Standing on the quay, watching the ramps lower, one sensed a long-awaited chapter closing.
